title: From Edison's incandescent bulb to CFLs and LEDs: history, power use and lifetime

sources.title: The History of the Light Bulb

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy (Solid-State Lighting Program; prepared by Navigant Consulting)
sources.title: Life-Cycle Assessment of Energy and Environmental Impacts of LED Lighting Products, Part I (February 2012, updated August 2012), Table 4.1, Table 4.7 and Figure 4.1
sources.note: 表格數字取自 Table 4.1（白熾燈、CFL、2011 年 LED）與 Table 4.7（鹵素燈）；CFL 壽命以 2012 年 8 月更正後的 8,500 小時為準

facts.text: Incandescent bulbs dominated the market for about 100 years.
About 90 percent of the energy an incandescent bulb uses is given off as heat and only about 10 percent as light.
Scientists worked on incandescent lamps for decades before Thomas Edison patented his incandescent bulb in 1879.
In October 1879, a carbonized cotton-thread filament tested by Edison's team lasted 14.5 hours.
Edison's team later used a bamboo filament that could last up to 1,200 hours.
In 1962, Nick Holonyak Jr. of General Electric invented the first LED that gave off visible light; it was red.
In 1976, Edward Hammer of General Electric made the first compact fluorescent lamp (CFL) by bending a fluorescent tube into a spiral.
General Electric shelved Hammer's CFL design because the machinery needed to mass-produce it was too expensive.
Early CFLs reached stores in the mid-1980s at prices of $25 to $35 each.
A CFL gives as much light as a comparable incandescent bulb but uses about 75 percent less energy and lasts up to 10 times longer.
LEDs use up to 90 percent less energy and last up to 25 times longer than incandescent bulbs; an LED can last up to 4 times longer than a CFL.
In the 2012 DOE comparison, an incandescent bulb used 60 watts, gave 900 lumens and lasted 1,000 hours.
In the 2012 DOE comparison, a halogen bulb used 43 watts, gave 750 lumens and lasted 1,000 hours.
In the 2012 DOE comparison, a CFL used 15 watts, gave 900 lumens and lasted 8,500 hours.
In the 2012 DOE comparison, a 2011 LED lamp used 12.5 watts, gave 800 lumens and lasted 25,000 hours.
To supply 20 million lumen-hours of light, a home would need about 22 incandescent bulbs, about 3 CFLs or about 1 LED lamp.
Lighting accounts for about 15 percent of an average U.S. home's electricity use.
In the table, the CFL uses a quarter of the incandescent bulb's power (15 of 60 watts) and the 2011 LED lasts 25 times as long as the incandescent bulb (25,000 versus 1,000 hours).

notes: 表格（Table 1）四列：Incandescent 60 W／900 lm／1,000 h；Halogen 43 W／750 lm／1,000 h；CFL 15 W／900 lm／8,500 h；LED (2011) 12.5 W／800 lm／25,000 h（DOE 2012 Table 4.1、4.7）。注意 DOE 2012 的 LED 是 800 lm，亮度略低於白熾燈與 CFL 的 900 lm，不可說成「亮度相同」。表格是 fact_only 來源的數字，不是 dataset（表格題不畫圖）。
